content: 1. Reports indicate that hyperglycemia can occur due to insulin resistance when protease inhibitors are used. Fosamprenavir reduces the efficacy of exenatide injectable suspension through mechanisms not fully understood. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments for drugs metabolized by CYP3A4 may be necessary. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of felodipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 5. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of fesoterodine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of finerenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Serum potassium should be monitored during initiation and dosage adjustments of finerenone or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 7. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while fludrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir through the same pathway. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of flurazepam by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Alternatives should be considered, and benzodiazepine doses may need to be lowered. 10. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of fluticasone furoate and fluticasone inhaled by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to fluticasone. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Fosaprepitant increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Co-administration of fosphenytoin and fosamprenavir may decrease the concentration of amprenavir, the active metabolite. However, when fosamprenavir is combined with ritonavir, an increased concentration of amprenavir is observed. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406, the major active metabolite of fostamatinib. 15. Fostamatinib increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Concomitant use may increase concentrations of P-gp substrates, requiring dosage reductions to avoid toxicities. 16. Garlic decreases the levels of fosamprenavir through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of gefitinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib-related adverse effects. 18. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of gepirone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both gepirone and fosamprenavir prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 19. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 20. Fosamprenavir reduces the effects of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide through mechanisms not fully understood. Caution and monitoring are advised. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. 21. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 22. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. FDA-approved labeling recommends halving the guanfacine dose when co-administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors. 24. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. 25. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism, while hydrocortisone decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir through the same pathway. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 26. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 28. Fosamprenavir decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active alkylating metabolites, potentially decreasing its therapeutic effectiveness. 29. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while iloperidone increases the levels of fosamprenavir through the same pathway. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Iloperidone, a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor, may elevate plasma levels of drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A4. 30. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of imipramine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of indinavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while indinavir increases the levels of fosamprenavir through the same pathway. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 32. Fosamprenavir reduces the effects of various forms of insulin (e.g., aspart, detemir, glargine, lispro) through mechanisms such as pharmacodynamic antagonism or insulin resistance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. HIV protease inhibitors may cause new-onset diabetes mellitus, exacerbate existing diabetes, and induce hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. 33. Fosamprenavir decreases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 34. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 35. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clinical trials have shown that istradefylline at 40 mg/day increases peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates, but this effect was not observed at 20 mg/day. 36. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Ivacaftor and its M1 metabolite may inhibit P-glycoprotein, significantly increasing systemic exposure to sensitive P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. 37. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 38. Fosamprenavir decreases the levels or effects of ketamine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of lacosamide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 40. Fosamprenavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 41. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 43. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Adverse effects should be monitored if lefamulin is co-administered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 45. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrate levels initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 46. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to amlodipine, requiring dose adjustments. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema. 47. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 48. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone concentrations. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 49. Fosamprenavir decreases the effects of linagliptin and liraglutide through mechanisms not fully understood. Caution and monitoring are advised. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. 50. Lomitapide increases the levels of fosamprenavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Consider reducing the dose when used concomitantly with lomitapide. 51. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 52. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of loratadine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Fosamprenavir increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Due to the induction effect of lumacaftor on CYP3A, the net exposure of ivacaftor at steady state is not expected to exceed that observed with ivacaftor monotherapy. No dose adjustment is necessary when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients taking lumacaftor/ivacaftor.
